fixes.explanation: That's it, baker. "All the kings of the earth sought an audience with Solomon to hear the wisdom that God had put in his heart." (2 Chronicles 9:23) Kings came from all over the earth just to listen. Picture a king showing up at the door for wisdom. I'd have shown up with a tray of cookies.

The gold and the ships are in the passage, so I see why you picked it. But the verse says the kings came "…to hear the wisdom that God had put in his heart." (2 Chronicles 9:23) The ships of Tarshish are mentioned two verses earlier (2 Chronicles 9:21), and they're not the reason given for the visits. The kings came for the wisdom, friend.
Right on the money, baker. "Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel forty years." (2 Chronicles 9:30) Forty years is a long time to hold a throne. That's a lot of mornings to be king.

Yes, baker. "…Solomon rested with his fathers and was buried in the city of his father David." (2 Chronicles 9:31) David reigned over all Israel before Solomon did (1 Chronicles 29:26), and he was Solomon's father. All that gold, and the passage ends with a burial. That tells you something big, friend.

Saul was made king at Gilgal (1 Samuel 11:15), but he's not Solomon's father. The verse says Solomon "…was buried in the city of his father David." (2 Chronicles 9:31) David, not Saul. Easy to mix up two names, friend.

Samuel anointed David with oil (1 Samuel 16:13), but he wasn't Solomon's father. The text says Solomon "…was buried in the city of his father David." (2 Chronicles 9:31) So the blank is David. Samuel's a good name to know, friend.

Abijah is a name from later in this book (2 Chronicles 13:1), but he isn't the one here. The verse says, "And his son Rehoboam reigned in his place." (2 Chronicles 9:31) So it's Rehoboam who takes over from Solomon. Keep that name handy, friend.
